answer_1.quote: Open-ended conversations (OEC) are the most common form of interaction between humans and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), representing a crucial feature of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).
answer_1.outputs: dialogue responses in multimodal open-ended conversations

answer_2.quote: Moreover, both GPT and human evaluators employ a scoring scale ranging from 0 to 5, with prompts and evaluation criteria detailed in the Appendix J. In contrast, for IE, IM, and AR, we employ objective precision metrics, including Extraction Precision (EP), Image Management Precision (IMP), and Refuse Precision (RP), to provide an intuitive assessment of model performance by measuring the proportion of correct responses.

answer_3.quote: MMRC also applies GPT-4o for scoring the model's information extraction, cross-turn reasoning, information update, image management, long-term memory recall, and answer refusal capabilities.

answer_4.quote: We also conduct manual evaluation of the capabilities in cross-turn reasoning, image update, and memory recall.
answer_4.guideline: The three evaluation criteria are as follows: (1) Cross-turn reasoning (CR): Full reasoning (5 points): the model accurately integrates information from multiple dialogue turns... (2) Information Update (IU): Complete Update (5 points): the model accurately and promptly updates new factual information... (3) Memory Recall (MR): Accurate Recall (5 points): the model accurately recalls key information (e.g., user preferences, previous conversation details)...
